answer: Shared-cost escrow anchoring. Each new identity must anchor a distinct escrow account funded at a fixed threshold, and the agent economy settles an identity's outbound obligations from that shared pool before it can transact. A clone therefore pays the full threshold with no offsetting revenue, a positive cost against near-zero expected gain — the oasis of liquidity requires a real deposit. Escrow idle time compounds via a slow glacier of holding charges, and any dispute spikes a gale of reserve top-ups. Marginal clones run strictly negative-EV.
